tasks.title: Helm save outcome: one conflict statement, the settle's own scroll target, a true test docblock
acceptance: C1 (one banner says it). A new test in src/renderer/src/helm/HelmPanel.test.tsx renders HelmPanel with `conflict` and `actionError` set to the same main-style sentence containing the word "changed" (for example 'settings.json changed on disk. Nothing was written.'), `stale: true` and `dirty: true`. Over the six banners HelmNotices renders, found by test id (PANEL_TEST_IDS.helmReadOnly, helmError, helmConflict, helmStale, helmBackupPath, and 'helm-unplaced-issues'; HelmNotices.tsx:92,104,120,150,161,171 at c40d1bb), it asserts that exactly one banner's textContent contains the substring "changed" and that this banner is helmConflict. Measured at c40d1bb in that state: 2 banners contain it (helm-conflict and helm-stale). Required after: 1. Red step: run the test before HelmNotices.tsx changes and report the failure.

C2 (main's sentence is not on screen). In the C1 state, a test asserts that main's sentence passed as `conflict` is rendered nowhere in the panel: the file's `occurrences(message)` helper returns 0 and helmConflict's textContent does not contain it. It also asserts that the substring "changed" occurs exactly once in helmConflict's textContent. Measured at c40d1bb: "changed" occurs 2 times in helmConflict (COPY.conflictLead at copy.ts:106, plus main's sentence rendered at HelmNotices.tsx:133). Red step required, as in C1.

C3 (the one statement is complete; preserved, newly tested). In the C1 state, a test asserts that helmConflict contains COPY.conflictLead, the selected scope's display path, and COPY.conflictAdvice, and holds exactly one HELM_SAFETY_TEST_IDS.compare button. All of these hold at c40d1bb by design. The criterion fixes them as the banner's whole statement now that main's sentence is gone. Demonstrated discrimination: remove the COPY.conflictAdvice paragraph from HelmNotices.tsx at one site, run the narrowest command that shows the failure, revert, and read the site back.

C4 (no stale banner beside a conflict). In the C1 state (`stale: true` with `conflict` non-null), a test asserts that PANEL_TEST_IDS.helmStale is absent. At c40d1bb it is present: HelmNotices.tsx:146 renders it whenever `stale` is true. Red step required. Per the orchestrator's assumption A2, the rule is a render rule in HelmNotices.tsx (the stale banner is not rendered while `conflict !== null`). src/renderer/src/state/panel-store.ts is not changed (see C11).

C5 (an on-disk change with no rejected save still warns; preserved). The existing test 'advises, offers Reload, and never disables Save' in describe('the stale banner') (HelmPanel.test.tsx:339 at c40d1bb, `stale: true`, `conflict: null`) keeps its name and assertions, and passes.

C6 (the stale banner comes back once the conflict is gone; preserved, newly tested). A new test renders the C1 state and then, through the file's `update` rerender, sets `conflict: null` and `actionError: null` and keeps `stale: true`. This is the state Discard leaves: panel-store.ts:701 clears `conflict` and does not touch `stale`. It asserts that helmStale is present and that helmConflict is absent. Demonstrated discrimination: at the single helmStale render site in HelmNotices.tsx, make the condition never true. Show that this test and the C5 test fail, revert, and read the site back.

C7 (end to end, with the real store). In src/renderer/src/__tests__/failure-paths.e2e.test.tsx, the test 'renders the conflict banner, keeps the draft, offers Reload, and lets a re-made edit save after it' (:1577 at c40d1bb) no longer asserts `within(banner).getByText(CONFLICT)` (:1597 at c40d1bb). After the rejected save it asserts that the conflict banner does not contain CONFLICT, that it contains COPY.conflictLead, and that PANEL_TEST_IDS.helmStale is absent. Each assertion is separate, so one failure is reported alone. The real store sets `stale: true` on a CONFLICT (panel-store.ts:744), so the helmStale assertion fails at c40d1bb. Red step required for it. Its other assertions keep their meaning.

C8. In src/renderer/src/__tests__/helm-draft-safety.e2e.test.tsx, 'keeps the typed model on screen when the save is rejected with CONFLICT' (:193 at c40d1bb) replaces `within(banner).getByText(CONFLICT_MESSAGE)` (:204 at c40d1bb) with an assertion that the banner does not contain CONFLICT_MESSAGE and does contain COPY.conflictLead. The test still asserts that the typed model survives, and it passes.

C9 (the probe stops requiring main's sentence). The PANEL_PROPERTIES entry 'a conflict names the file, says nothing was written, and keeps the draft' in src/renderer/src/helm/probes.ts no longer fails when main's sentence is absent from the conflict banner. `grep -c "the conflict message was not shown verbatim" /c/Users/dmarq/Development/Repos/orcastrate/.claude-worktrees/20261118-2121-helm-save-outcome-followups/src/renderer/src/helm/probes.ts` prints 0 (it prints 1 at c40d1bb, :236). The entry still checks 'nothing was written', the file name, the editable draft and the single Reload. Every PANEL_PROPERTIES name is unchanged, so src/renderer/src/helm/discrimination.test.tsx, which this task does not own, passes unmodified.

C10 (HelmNotices says what it now does). The file docblock and the inline comment in src/renderer/src/helm/HelmNotices.tsx (:1-16 and :71-79 at c40d1bb) state that a rejected save's message from main is not rendered, and that COPY.conflictLead plus COPY.conflictAdvice is the conflict banner's statement. They also state that the stale banner is not rendered while a conflict banner is. The paragraph 'THE MESSAGE MAIN WROTE IS THE MESSAGE ON SCREEN' names this exception instead of claiming that every `actionError` is printed verbatim. Neither text says the conflict banner prints main's message.

C11 (assumptions A1 and A2: main and the store are unchanged; preserved). `git -C /c/Users/dmarq/Development/Repos/orcastrate/.claude-worktrees/20261118-2121-helm-save-outcome-followups diff --quiet c40d1bb -- src/main/helm/helm-service.ts src/renderer/src/state/panel-store.ts` exits 0. The reviewer runs it; implementers run no git.

C12 (row 40, success over a leftover error). A new test in the describe('when a save settles') block of HelmPanel.test.tsx renders `saving: true` with a leftover scope-listing failure: `phase: 'error'` and `error: ipcError('IO', ...)`, with the fixture's document and draft kept. It then rerenders with `saving: false` and a `lastSave` whose scope is the one on screen. It asserts that scrollIntoView ran exactly once, on an element that contains PANEL_TEST_IDS.helmBackupPath and does not contain helmError. Measured at c40d1bb, the call's element was helm-error. Red step required.

C13 (a conflict over a leftover error). The same setup as C12, settling instead with `conflict` and `actionError` set to the same sentence and `stale: true`. The test asserts one scrollIntoView call, on an element that contains helmConflict and not helmError. Measured at c40d1bb, the element was helm-error. Red step required.

C14 (a failure is not scrolled to an earlier Saved; preserved, newly tested). A new test starts with `saving: true` and a `lastSave` for the scope on screen, so helmBackupPath is rendered. It settles with `saving: false` and `actionError: 'ENOSPC: no space left on device, write'`. It asserts one scrollIntoView call, on an element that contains helmError and not helmBackupPath. Measured at c40d1bb, the element was helm-error. Demonstrated discrimination: at the single site where the target banner is chosen, make helmBackupPath win whenever it is on screen. Show that this test fails, revert, and read the site back.

C15 (a conflict is not scrolled to an earlier Saved; preserved, newly tested). The same start as C14, settling with `conflict` and `actionError` set to the same sentence. The test asserts one call, on an element that contains helmConflict and not helmBackupPath. Measured at c40d1bb, the element was helm-conflict. Demonstrated discrimination: the same injection as C14, which must fail this test as well.

C16 (a later failure is not scrolled to an earlier conflict; preserved, newly tested). A new test starts with `saving: true` and `conflict` set, so helmConflict is rendered. It settles with `saving: false` and `actionError: 'ENOSPC: no space left on device, write'`, with `conflict` still set. The store keeps `current.conflict` on a non-CONFLICT failure (panel-store.ts:745). The test asserts one call, on an element that contains helmError and not helmConflict. Measured at c40d1bb, the element was helm-error. Demonstrated discrimination: at the target-choice site, make helmConflict win whenever `conflict` is non-null. Show that this test fails, revert, and read the site back.

C17 (the existing settle tests; preserved). The 7 tests in describe('when a save settles') at c40d1bb (HelmPanel.test.tsx:423-487) keep their names and assertions, and all pass: 'scrolls the Saved banner into view once the save lands', 'scrolls the error banner into view when the save fails', 'scrolls the conflict banner into view when the save is rejected', 'does not scroll on a first render that already shows a Saved banner', 'does not scroll on a re-render where no save was in flight', 'does not scroll when a save settles with no outcome banner on screen', and 'does not scroll when the save that settled belongs to a file not on screen'.

C18 (the hook's docblock states the new rule). The file docblock and the selector comment in src/renderer/src/helm/useSaveOutcomeScroll.ts say which banner each settle scrolls to: a save that landed goes to Saved (helmBackupPath), a save rejected with a conflict goes to the conflict banner, and any other failed save goes to the error banner. They say that nothing scrolls when that banner is not on screen. The 'WHY THIS IS ITS OWN FILE' paragraph is kept. `grep -c "first save-outcome banner" /c/Users/dmarq/Development/Repos/orcastrate/.claude-worktrees/20261118-2121-helm-save-outcome-followups/src/renderer/src/helm/useSaveOutcomeScroll.ts` prints 0 (1 at c40d1bb, :5), and no text in the file says the first match in DOM order wins.

C19 (encodes the project lesson at .sir/lessons.md:102, enforced by the source rule at src/renderer/src/helm/rules.ts:172 through src/renderer/src/helm/no-paths.test.ts; preserved). `grep -cE "use(Effect|LayoutEffect|Memo)\(" /c/Users/dmarq/Development/Repos/orcastrate/.claude-worktrees/20261118-2121-helm-save-outcome-followups/src/renderer/src/helm/HelmPanel.tsx` prints 0 (0 at c40d1bb). The same command with the pattern `\bcompare\(\)` prints 0 on src/renderer/src/helm/useSaveOutcomeScroll.ts (0 at c40d1bb). As a control it prints 1 on HelmPanel.tsx (1 at c40d1bb), which shows that the instrument fires. src/renderer/src/helm/no-paths.test.ts passes.

C20 (encodes the frontend discipline rule 'Derived values are computed, never stored'; preserved). The banner a settle scrolls to is derived from the view on the settling render and is not kept in state. `grep -oE '\buse(State|Ref|Reducer)[<(]' <file> | wc -l` prints 2 for src/renderer/src/helm/HelmPanel.tsx and 1 for src/renderer/src/helm/useSaveOutcomeScroll.ts, the counts at c40d1bb (HelmPanel.tsx:64,96 and useSaveOutcomeScroll.ts:46). `grep -oE '\buse[A-Z][A-Za-z]*[<(]' src/renderer/src/helm/HelmNotices.tsx | wc -l` prints 0 (0 at c40d1bb), so HelmNotices still calls no hook. Run each command against the absolute worktree path.

C21 (row 41). `grep -n "the only component" /c/Users/dmarq/Development/Repos/orcastrate/.claude-worktrees/20261118-2121-helm-save-outcome-followups/src/renderer/src/helm/HelmPanel.test.tsx` prints nothing (1 line at c40d1bb, :9). The replacement text must therefore not use that phrase. The rewritten docblock still says why these tests need no provider and no stub bridge: HelmPanel takes everything through props. It claims no fact about hooks in src/renderer/src/helm that a grep of that directory contradicts. HelmPanel.tsx calls useState, useRef and useSaveOutcomeScroll. useRowFocus.ts:41 and HelmCloseConfirm.tsx:53 run useLayoutEffect. Among the non-test files, only ConnectedHelmPanel.tsx:28-29 calls useHelm()/useHelmActions().

C22 (no session id or session path in source). `grep -cE '20[0-9]{6}-[0-9]{4}-|20[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}-[a-z]|\.sir/sessions' <file>`, run on each owned file at its absolute worktree path, prints no more than it does at c40d1bb. The c40d1bb counts are HelmNotices.tsx 0, useSaveOutcomeScroll.ts 0, HelmPanel.tsx 2, HelmPanel.test.tsx 1, probes.ts 2, failure-paths.e2e.test.tsx 3, and helm-draft-safety.e2e.test.tsx 1. Text this task adds states each rule in place.
